gdp_level.source: Census and Statistics Department (C&SD), table 310-31001 · GDP at current market prices, HK$ million, not seasonally adjusted, quarterly.
gdp_level.description: The total value of everything Hong Kong produces in a year, at current prices, on a rolling four-quarter basis.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to C&SD's GDP in chained (2024) dollars, also quarterly. This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each quarter at that period's own HKD/USD rate (monthly, FRED DEXHKUS). The HK dollar has been linked to the US dollar since 1983, so this changes the level, not the shape.

gdp_real.source: Census and Statistics Department (C&SD), table 310-31001 · GDP in chained (2024) dollars, HK$ million, not seasonally adjusted, quarterly.
gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current prices instead.
gdp_real.dollar: With “Make it real” on, “Dollarise” converts every period at one rate, the average for the latest year, so dollar growth equals real growth.

gdp_growth.source: Census and Statistics Department (C&SD), table 310-31001 · real GDP, seasonally adjusted, change on the previous quarter, as published.
gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous three months, in real terms, with regular seasonal patterns removed.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying HK dollars to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

gdp_growth_yoy.source: Census and Statistics Department (C&SD), table 310-31001 · real GDP, change on the same quarter a year earlier, as published.
gdp_growth_yoy.description: How much bigger or smaller the economy is than a year earlier, adjusted for inflation. This is C&SD's headline growth figure.
gdp_growth_yoy.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying HK dollars to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

cpi.source: IMF consumer price index (CPI, HKG.CPI._T.YOY_PCH_PA_PT.M), from the Census and Statistics Department · Composite CPI, all items, change on the same month a year earlier as the IMF publishes it, to one decimal place, monthly.
cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago. Headline inflation swings when one-off government relief measures, such as rates or rent waivers, start and end.

cpi_mom.source: IMF consumer price index (CPI, HKG.CPI._T.POP_PCH_PA_PT.M) · Composite CPI, all items, change on the previous month, not seasonally adjusted, to one decimal place.
cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices changed in the latest month.

policy_rate.source: BIS central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL, M.HK, extended with the daily series D.HK) · the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's base rate, end of month, from October 1998; the current month shows the latest rate.
policy_rate.description: The base rate, the rate at which the Hong Kong Monetary Authority lends to banks overnight. Under the link to the US dollar it follows the US federal funds rate.

unemployment.source: World Bank SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS · International Labour Organization modelled estimate, % of the labour force, annual.
unemployment.description: The share of the labour force that wants a job and is actively looking, but can't find one. This is the ILO's modelled estimate, not the statistics office's own survey rate.

exports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · exports of goods including re-exports, free on board, US$ converted to HK dollars at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
exports.description: The value of goods Hong Kong sells to the rest of the world each month, in HK dollars.
exports.dollar: The IMF's figures are in US dollars; the HK dollars shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at the month's rate.

imports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · imports of goods, cost, insurance and freight, US$ converted to HK dollars at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
imports.description: The value of goods Hong Kong buys from the rest of the world each month, in HK dollars.
imports.dollar: The IMF's figures are in US dollars; the HK dollars shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at the month's rate.

trade_balance.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG) · exports less imports of goods, converted to HK dollars at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods. A negative number is a trade deficit.
trade_balance.dollar: The IMF's figures are in US dollars; the HK dollars shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at the month's rate.

debt_gdp.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXWDG_NGDP) · general government gross debt, % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
debt_gdp.description: Everything government owes, across all levels of government, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

deficit.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXCNL_NGDP) · general government net lending (+) or borrowing (-), % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
deficit.description: The gap between what government takes in and what it spends in a year, across all levels of government. A negative number is a deficit.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

current_account.source: World Bank BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS · current account balance, % of GDP, annual.
current_account.description: The balance of trade in goods and services plus income and transfers with the rest of the world. A negative number means the country is borrowing from abroad.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fdi.source: World Bank BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS · foreign direct investment, net inflows, % of GDP, annual.
fdi.description: Long-term investment into the country by foreign companies and investors, such as building factories or buying a lasting stake in a business.
fdi.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fx_usd.source: FRED series DEXHKUS (Federal Reserve H.10) · end-of-month rate, the current month shows the latest daily rate; shown as US$ per HK$1, 1 ÷ the published HKD per US$.
fx_usd.description: How many US dollars one HK dollar buys. The HK dollar is linked to the US dollar, held between 7.75 and 7.85 per US dollar since 2005, so this barely moves.
